.qc-cache/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r2/task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md, tests/gates/*/prompt.md, tests/scored/{polish,visual}/prompt.md, tests/app_context.md, all tests/**/judge.toml (criterion ids and text for overlap comparison)
evidence: Applied the skill's procedure (quality-checks.md #5): grep of instruction.md, environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md and integration.md for judge|rubric|criteri|dimension|reward|weight|score|playwright|claude|glm|/tests|sentinel|gate|probe|functional|polish|visual|verifier|grader|grading|oracle|harbor|app_context|test.sh|check returned exactly one hit: instruction.md:13 'expose GET /api/health as a check that never touches the database' - ordinary health-endpoint product language, not grader machinery. No hits in seed_data.json. No criterion id prefix 'hro_' (all ids in tests/**/judge.toml use it, e.g. hro_job_open, hro_bulk_move, hro_gate_render) appears in the brief, notes or seed. The brief does not name the judge model, Playwright, restart_app, the gates, the functional/polish/visual dimensions, the 0.6/0.2/0.2 weights, /tests paths, or the 'NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation' sentinel used in tests prompts. The judge prompts use no fixed probe literal (functional/prompt.md:15 requires per-review suffixed titles/names), so there is no GATE-PROBE-style value to leak. Verbatim overlap: an 8-word-shingle comparison of the public brief+notes against all 61 criterion texts/prompts found only two 8-word runs, both natural restatements of public requirements ('place the reason is shown and keyboard focus' in hro_refused_put_back vs hireops_rules.md:85; 'arrive at the bottom of that stage in' in hro_bulk_move vs hireops_rules.md:90) - the criteria quote the rule, the brief does not quote grader text, and the brief remains a natural user ask. Test files are not copied into the agent image (environment/Dockerfile COPY only instructions/ and assets/). Counterexample search: a broken app gains nothing from this row since no grader detail is exposed to target; a conforming alternative is not penalised because nothing in the brief steers toward judge-specific routes/selectors (hireops_rules.md:3-5 explicitly leaves routes, ids and labels to the builder). Template brief/notes are CHANGE_ME placeholders, so all task text is task-authored and reviewable. No runtime evidence is required for this static-text row; the private check-instruction-hygiene.py executable was not run here (that belongs to the deterministic reviewer), and this manual review is not presented as that checker's output.
